title: A partition-sensitivity display for shared effect modifiers is stable exactly when every candidate partition is wrong
question: Does the choice of which treatments share an effect-modifier interaction move a target contrast, does the widest estimable partition fail silently, and does the range over defensible partitions contain the truth?
design: A network with individual data on A vs B and aggregate trials of A vs C and A vs D; interaction heterogeneity within and between classes; three admissible partitions fitted by generalized least squares. 6 cells, 4000 replicates each.
answer: No. When an aggregate-only treatment's interaction differed from both candidate classes' (by 0.3) while theirs agreed, every admissible partition returned the same answer biased by -0.30; the range over partitions was narrow (0.14), contained the truth in 5% of replicates, and the only available fit test rejected at its nominal 5%. The widest partition covered 0.37. The range widened and contained the correct partition only when the candidate classes disagreed with each other.
findings: Widest partition bias -0.30 and coverage 0.37 at the primary cell, with the fit test rejecting in 5% of analyses.
The fit test detects disagreement between treatments with identified interactions (41% when C differs from B) and never the aggregate-only treatment's own departure.
With the candidate classes disagreeing, {B}{CD} or {BD}{C} was unbiased when D truly shared that class's interaction.
not_answered: Small hand-built network, continuous outcome, linear modification, three partitions, sufficient statistics drawn directly; no overlap factor or ML-NMR fits. Peer review has not been done.
estimand: D versus A mean difference at the target covariate mean
methods_compared: network fits under three admissible shared-modifier partitions
